title: nf-core reference genome configs (igenomes.config), nf-core/references datasheets, and AWS iGenomes
maintainer: nf-core community (nf-core/tools template, pipelines, nf-core/references); AWS iGenomes S3 mirror set up by Phil Ewels (SciLifeLab NGI), now maintained by nf-core; underlying data from Illumina iGenomes

formats.description: Groovy params.genomes map in an nf-core pipeline's conf/igenomes.config (from the nf-core/tools pipeline template). One record per genome key; the key is the value users pass as --genome. Two syntaxes exist: a map literal (current template, rnaseq, sarek) and a nested config block (methylseq, atacseq, chipseq, AWS-iGenomes example config).
formats.record_key: genome (the map key) within one pipeline's config

formats.description: nf-core/references asset datasheet: a YAML list, one entry per genome, listing the files (and a few tool values) available for it. Published in nf-core/references-datasheets (igenomes/, genomes/, genomes_source/) and validated by schema_references.json in the nf-core/references pipeline.
formats.record_key: species + reference_source + genome (the pipeline publishes to <species>/<reference_source>/<genome>/); genome alone is meta.id

formats.description: AWS iGenomes file manifest (ngi-igenomes_file_manifest.txt): one s3:// URI per line, one record per file. The adapter splits each URI along the iGenomes layout igenomes/<species>/<source>/<build>/<section>/<subpath>.

Illumina iGenomes GenomeSize.xml (Sequence/WholeGenomeFasta/GenomeSize.xml): a <sequenceSizes genomeName=...> root with one <chromosome .../> element per sequence. One record per <chromosome>, with the root genomeName repeated on each record.

Sequence dictionary served with each iGenomes FASTA (genome.dict; Homo_sapiens_assembly38.dict for GATK builds): SAM header @HD and @SQ lines (SAM spec, hts-specs). One record per @SQ line; @HD values are repeated on each record under '@HD/<tag>' keys.

FASTA index served with each iGenomes FASTA (genome.fa.fai): samtools/htslib faidx format, 5 tab-separated columns, no header. One record per sequence. Column names are the ones htslib's faidx(5) man page uses.
Annotation/README.txt in some iGenomes builds: free text saying when and from where the annotation was downloaded (and, for some builds, the Ensembl and miRBase release). Prose only; no adapter.
formats.record_key: the file's own path (one README per build)

fields.description: The params.genomes map key; the value users pass as --genome (e.g. GRCh38, hg38, R64-1-1, GATK.GRCh38).
fields.notes: Not a field inside the entry: the adapter stores the map key under 'genome' because that is the pipeline parameter that selects it (params.genome). Unique only within one pipeline's igenomes.config. The same key can point to different builds in different pipelines: rnaseq/methylseq/atacseq 'GRCh38' is the iGenomes NCBI/GRCh38 build, while sarek has no plain 'GRCh38' and uses 'NCBI.GRCh38' and 'GATK.GRCh38'. 'hg38' is the iGenomes UCSC/hg38 build everywhere.

fields.description: Path to the whole-genome FASTA file.
fields.notes: Path template; '${params.igenomes_base}' (default s3://ngi-igenomes/igenomes) is substituted by Nextflow at run time. In the AWS-iGenomes example config, fasta points to the WholeGenomeFasta directory, not the file. Equivalent datasheet field: fasta.

fields.description: Directory (or prefix) of the BWA index.
fields.notes: Path template; '${params.igenomes_base}' (default s3://ngi-igenomes/igenomes) is substituted by Nextflow at run time. Index files derived from the FASTA. iGenomes builds usually keep it under BWAIndex/version0.6.0/; the AWS-iGenomes example config points at the prefix .../BWAIndex/genome.fa. Datasheet equivalent: bwamem1_index.

fields.description: Directory (or prefix) of the Bowtie2 index.
fields.notes: Path template; '${params.igenomes_base}' (default s3://ngi-igenomes/igenomes) is substituted by Nextflow at run time. Datasheet equivalent: bowtie2_index.

fields.description: Directory of the STAR index.
fields.notes: Path template; '${params.igenomes_base}' (default s3://ngi-igenomes/igenomes) is substituted by Nextflow at run time. iGenomes STAR indexes were built with STAR 2.5.1b (see AWS-iGenomes README). Datasheet equivalent: star_index.

fields.description: Flag telling nf-core/rnaseq that the iGenomes STAR index was built with an old STAR version, so the pipeline uses a matching older STAR to read it.
fields.notes: rnaseq only. Describes the index copy, not the genome. Meaning inferred from the key name and rnaseq usage; not documented in the config itself.

fields.description: Directory of the Bismark (bisulfite) index.
fields.notes: Path template; '${params.igenomes_base}' (default s3://ngi-igenomes/igenomes) is substituted by Nextflow at run time. Datasheet equivalent: bismark_index (igenomes/ sheets; not in schema).

fields.description: Path to the gene annotation GTF.
fields.notes: Path template; '${params.igenomes_base}' (default s3://ngi-igenomes/igenomes) is substituted by Nextflow at run time. Annotation file in this build's naming style. iGenomes annotation is old (human Ensembl release 75 era per nf-core docs).

fields.description: Path to genes in BED12 format (made from the GTF with gtf2bed).
fields.notes: Path template; '${params.igenomes_base}' (default s3://ngi-igenomes/igenomes) is substituted by Nextflow at run time. Datasheet equivalents: genes_bed (igenomes/ sheets) and bed12 (schema).

fields.description: Name of the mitochondrial sequence in this build's naming style.
fields.notes: Same genome can use 'chrM' (UCSC-style, also iGenomes NCBI/GRCh38) or 'MT' (Ensembl-style). Depends on the sequence collection, not the assembly.

fields.description: Effective genome size passed to MACS2 (-g), as a quoted number string.
fields.notes: rnaseq/methylseq/template: a string such as '2.7e9' or '1.2e7'. atacseq/chipseq use a map keyed by read length instead (see macs_gsize.<len>). Approximate, depends on mappability, so not an identifier.

fields.description: Path to a region blacklist BED shipped inside the pipeline (assets/blacklists).
fields.notes: Uses ${projectDir} (the pipeline's own folder), not igenomes_base. Same file can serve two keys (GRCh38 and hg38 both use hg38-blacklist.bed) even though their chromosome naming may differ.

fields.description: Directory of the BWA-MEM2 index.
fields.notes: Path template; '${params.igenomes_base}' (default s3://ngi-igenomes/igenomes) is substituted by Nextflow at run time. Datasheet equivalent: bwamem2_index.

fields.description: Path or URL to a GFF3 gene annotation.
fields.notes: In rnaseq it appears only for CHM13 and is an absolute NCBI FTP URL, not an iGenomes path.

fields.description: Path to the iGenomes Annotation/README.txt for this build.
fields.notes: Path template; '${params.igenomes_base}' (default s3://ngi-igenomes/igenomes) is substituted by Nextflow at run time. Present only for builds that ship a README (e.g. sacCer3, not GRCh38). Content is prose; see format nfcore_igenomes_readme.

fields.description: Name of the genome build (e.g. GRCh38, hg38, R64-1-1, GRCh38.p14, GRCh38_chr21). Becomes meta.id in the pipeline.
fields.notes: The only required field. Unique only together with species and reference_source: 'GRCh38' appears under NCBI and GATK, 'hg38' under UCSC and GATK. In igenomes/ sheets it equals the iGenomes <build> folder; it does not always equal the --genome key of pipeline configs (sarek uses 'GATK.GRCh38').

fields.description: Genome FASTA path or URL (may be gzipped).
fields.notes: Path template; '${params.references_base_path}' (default s3://ngi-igenomes/igenomes) is substituted when the datasheet loads. genomes_source/ sheets use absolute URLs. In genomes_source/ sheets it is the upstream download URL (NCBI analysis set, Gencode primary assembly), so it identifies which sequence collection is meant.

fields.description: Who provides this build: NCBI, UCSC, Ensembl, GATK, Gencode, Illumina, nf-core.
fields.notes: Equals the iGenomes <source> path segment for igenomes/ sheets. Tells naming style and content (e.g. NCBI iGenomes GRCh38 uses chr names). Renamed from 'source' in the older pipeline schema.

fields.description: Species, capitalized with underscore (e.g. Homo_sapiens, Saccharomyces_cerevisiae).

fields.description: samtools .fai index of the FASTA.

The dict carries per-sequence MD5s (M5) and is the best digest source in this ecosystem; see format nfcore_igenomes_dict.

fields.description: Root attribute of <sequenceSizes>: free-text name of the build, e.g. 'Homo Sapiens (NCBI GRCh38)'.
fields.notes: Repeated on every record by the adapter. Free text with inconsistent capitalization ('Homo Sapiens' vs 'Homo sapiens'); format is roughly '<species> (<source> <build>)'.

fields.description: FASTA file name the sequence is in (always genome.fa in the examples).
fields.notes: Relative to the WholeGenomeFasta folder.

fields.description: Sequence name as written in the FASTA.
fields.notes: Unique within one file. Naming style follows the build (chr1 for UCSC and iGenomes NCBI/GRCh38; I, II, MT for Ensembl R64-1-1).

fields.description: Sequence length in bases.
fields.notes: Same as fai LENGTH and dict LN.

fields.description: Build name (only in some files, e.g. NCBI/GRCh38: 'GRCh38').
Whether the sequence is circular.
fields.notes: Not reliable: 'false' for every sequence in the examples, including chrM/MT.

fields.description: MD5 of the sequence.
fields.notes: Equals the M5 in the same build's genome.dict. For iGenomes NCBI/GRCh38 it matches the standard SAM M5 (and GATK GRCh38). For iGenomes UCSC/hg38, 14 of 195 sequences (chr1, chr2, ...) have a different md5 than NCBI/GRCh38 despite equal names, lengths and knownBases; cause not determined, so do not assume it equals a refget/UCSC md5 without checking. Yeast R64-1-1 and sacCer3 md5s match each other.

fields.description: Ploidy of the sequence.
fields.notes: Not reliable: 2 for every sequence in the examples, including chrM and haploid-yeast sequences.

fields.description: Species with underscore (only in some files, e.g. 'Homo_sapiens').
Number of non-N bases (believed).
fields.notes: Inferred, not documented: chrM has totalBases 16569 and knownBases 16568, matching the single N in the rCRS sequence.

fields.description: Sequence role: Autosome, Allosome, Mitochondria, Contig, Unknown (only in some files).
fields.notes: Only in NCBI/GRCh38 among the anchors. chrEBV is 'Unknown'; unlocalized/unplaced scaffolds are 'Contig'.

fields.description: SAM format version from the @HD line (e.g. 1.0, 1.5).
fields.notes: Header line value repeated on every record by the adapter.

fields.description: Sort order from the @HD line (always 'unsorted' in dicts).
fields.notes: Header line value repeated on every record by the adapter.

fields.description: Reference sequence name (@SQ SN).
fields.notes: Unique within one dict.

fields.description: Reference sequence length (@SQ LN).
URI or path of the FASTA the dict was made from (@SQ UR).
fields.notes: Records where the dict was built, not where the file is now: e.g. file:/illumina/scratch/iGenomes/..., file:C:\Genomes\..., /seq/references/Homo_sapiens_assembly38/v0/... (Broad).

fields.description: MD5 of the sequence (@SQ M5); SAM spec: uppercase, whitespace removed.
fields.notes: See md5 notes in nfcore_igenomes_genomesize: iGenomes UCSC/hg38 values differ from NCBI/GRCh38 for 14 sequences.

fields.description: Genome assembly identifier (@SQ AS); '38' in the GATK GRCh38 dict.
fields.notes: Only in the GATK dict among the examples. Short and not an accession.

fields.description: Species (@SQ SP), e.g. 'Homo sapiens'.
fields.notes: Only in the GATK dict among the examples.

fields.description: Sequence name (same as SN in the dict).
fields.notes: Unique within one file.

fields.description: Sequence length in bases.
Byte offset of the sequence's first base in the FASTA file.
fields.notes: Depends on the exact file bytes (header text, line width).

fields.description: Bases per FASTA line.
fields.notes: Line width of this copy; differs between copies of the same sequences: iGenomes NCBI/GRCh38 70, UCSC/hg38 50, GATK GRCh38 100, Ensembl R64-1-1 60, UCSC sacCer3 50.

fields.description: Bytes per FASTA line including the newline.
Whole file text, e.g. 'The contents of this directory were downloaded from UCSC on: March 6, 2013'.

fields.notes: Prose; carries the download date and provider, and for Ensembl builds the Ensembl and miRBase release numbers (example in spec/nfcore_docs/reference-genomes.md). No adapter.
